```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Load data
df = pd.read_csv('chunks_csv/bivariate/bivariate_2023_ghg_crime.csv')
adj_df = pd.read_csv('chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv')

# Create adjacency dictionary
adj_dict = {}
for borough in df['borough']:
    adj_dict[borough] = set(adj_df[adj_df['borough'] == borough]['neighbor'])

# Create spatial weights matrix (binary)
boroughs = df['borough'].values
n = len(boroughs)
W = np.zeros((n, n))
for i, b1 in enumerate(boroughs):
    for j, b2 in enumerate(boroughs):
        if b2 in adj_dict[b1]:
            W[i,j] = 1

# Standardize rows (row-normalize)
W = W / W.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
W = np.nan_to_num(W)  # handle boroughs with no neighbors

print("Spatial weights matrix created")
```

```python
X_std = (X - X.mean()) / X.std()
Y_std = (Y - Y.mean()) / Y.std()

# Calculate Lee's L
n = len(X)
S0 = W.sum()
L = (X_std @ W @ Y_std) / S0

# Permutation test
n_perm = 500
perm_stats = np.zeros(n_perm)
for i in range(n_perm):
    Y_perm = np.random.permutation(Y_std)
    perm_stats[i] = (X_std @ W @ Y_perm) / S0

# Calculate p-value
p_value = (np.sum(perm_stats >= L) + 1) / (n_perm + 1)  # +1 for observed value

print(f"Lee's L: {L:.4f}, p-value: {p_value:.4f}")
```
